classification.difficultyReason: Find an unstated radius using Pythagoras, then combine two triangle areas with a sector area.

content.prompt: Find the area of the composite shape to 2 d.p.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 6 diagram below the prompt on the left
spec.description: An unshaded composite outline with a horizontal base, equal vertical sides and a circular arc. Dashed equal radii join the base midpoint to the arc endpoints.
spec.mathematics: The base is 8 mm and both vertical sides are 3 mm. The radii are equal and meet at the base midpoint. Preserve the source's stated 106° angle, its angle marker, double ticks on the vertical sides and single ticks on the radii. Coordinates derived from the lengths give radius 5 mm and an angle approximately 106°.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens appear: 8 mm, 3 mm and 106°. The radius and area are withheld.

answer.worked:
Half the base is $4\text{ mm}$. Using a right-angled triangle:
$$\begin{align*}r&=\sqrt{4^2+3^2}\\r&=5\text{ mm}\end{align*}$$
Add the areas of the two triangles and the sector.
$$\begin{align*}A&=2\left(\frac12\times3\times4\right)+\frac{106}{360}\pi(5)^2\\A&=12+\frac{265\pi}{36}\\A&\approx35.13\text{ mm}^2\end{align*}$$
